c.tagline: City of Prophets, sacred carp pools, and the world's oldest temple.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are yellow and metered; apps like BiTaksi and Uber simply hail a licensed metered taxi rather than a private car. Confirm the meter (taksimetre) is running at the start of the ride.

emergency.note: 112 is Türkiye's unified emergency number, connecting to police, ambulance, and fire services.

avoid.reason: Southeast near the Syria border — heightened security risk; check advisories before travel

hood_desc: The sacred heart of the old city around Balıklıgöl, the pool of sacred carp tied to the legend of Abraham, framed by the Halil-ür Rahman and Rızvaniye mosques and their gardens; the atmospheric core where stone konak (mansion) hotels put you steps from the main sights.

The archaeology district just west of Balıklıgöl, home to the vast Şanlıurfa Archæology Museum — which displays finds from Göbekli Tepe — and the Haleplibahçe Mosaic Museum with its Amazon-queen floors; a sightseeing base rich in the city's ancient story.

Şanlıurfa's modern northern district of wide avenues, shopping malls, parks, and newer international-brand hotels; suits travelers who want quieter, contemporary accommodation away from the crowded old town.

The commercial city centre around Sarayönü Caddesi, dense with shops, kebab houses, banks, and mid-range hotels; a convenient, well-connected central base within walking distance of the bazaar and Balıklıgöl.

water.note: Stick to bottled water, as locals largely do.

transit.hours: City buses and shared minibuses run from around 6:00 AM to about 11:00 PM.
transit.note: Şanlıurfa has no metro or tram; the municipal bus network and shared dolmuş minibuses are the main public transport, backed up by cheap yellow taxis and ride-hailing apps that dispatch licensed taxis.
transit.pay: Buses use the rechargeable UrfaKart smart card, tapped on boarding and topped up at kiosks and machines; dolmuş minibuses are paid in cash to the driver.

bus: Intercity coaches from the otogar to Gaziantep, Diyarbakır, and beyond
Dolmuş minibuses to Harran and nearby towns

transit.m: Shuttle or municipal bus to the city center (~40 min)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving about 5-10% for good service in restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory.

landmarks: Göbekli Tepe
The world's oldest known temple complex, a UNESCO-listed hilltop sanctuary of carved megaliths raised 11,500 years ago, rewriting the story of civilisation itself.
Balıklıgöl (Pool of Sacred Fish)
A serene sacred pool teeming with protected carp, where tradition says God turned Nimrod's fire to water and the flames' embers into fish saving Abraham.
Mevlid-i Halil Mosque and Cave of Abraham
A revered mosque complex enclosing the cave where Islamic tradition holds the Prophet Abraham was born, drawing pilgrims from across the Muslim world.
Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum
Türkiye's largest archaeology museum, showcasing the haunting 11,000-year-old Urfa Man statue and superb finds from Göbekli Tepe and the Neolithic Euphrates.
Haleplibahçe Mosaic Museum
A dome-covered treasury of dazzling Roman-era floor mosaics, including hunting Amazon queens, preserved exactly where a wealthy Edessa villa once stood.
Şanlıurfa Castle (Urfa Kalesi)
A ruined citadel crowned by two Corinthian columns, the 'Throne of Nimrod', offering sweeping views over Balıklıgöl and the old city's minarets.
Rızvaniye Mosque and Ayn Zeliha Lake
An elegant 18th-century Ottoman mosque and madrasa arcade reflected in Balıklıgöl's waters, beside the tranquil spring-fed lake named for Nimrod's daughter.
Gümrük Han and the Old Bazaar
A bustling 16th-century caravanserai courtyard where tea drinkers and backgammon players gather amid labyrinthine bazaars scented with isot pepper and roasted pistachios.
Great Mosque of Urfa (Ulu Cami)
A 12th-century Zengid mosque built over a Byzantine church, its octagonal bell-tower-turned-minaret presiding over a peaceful courtyard of ancient plane trees.
On Gözlü Köprü (Ten-Eyed Bridge)
A ten-arched stone bridge spanning the Karakoyun stream on the edge of the old city, built during the medieval Ayyubid period and still in daily use.

train.note: Şanlıurfa has no passenger rail service yet; a high-speed line linking it to Gaziantep is under construction. The nearest working stations are at Gaziantep and Karkamış, both a couple of hours away by road, so the coach is the practical way in and out.

bus.note: No international coaches - the Syrian border here is not open to ordinary travellers. Frequent intercity coaches run from Şanlıurfa's otogar to Gaziantep (about 2 hours), Diyarbakır, Mardin and Adana, with overnight services to Ankara and Istanbul on Metro Turizm (https://www.metroturizm.com.tr/en) and regional carriers; book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/).

ferry.note: Şanlıurfa is inland with no coast. Boat trips do run on Atatürk Dam lake and Halfeti on the Euphrates nearby, but these are excursions rather than scheduled transport.

full.blurb: Partly submerged 'sunken village' on the Euphrates, visited by boat past drowned minarets, with its rare dark-purple roses.
